sections.h2: What does the Madison County Judge of Probate do with a deed?
sections.html:
The Madison County Judge of Probate is the office where deeds and mortgages are recorded, and a deed does not give a buyer public notice of ownership until it is filed there. The recording office is at the Madison County Service Center, 1918 Memorial Parkway NW, Huntsville, the same building that houses the tax collector and the Board of Equalization.

Alabama counties handle several jobs that other states split between offices. The probate judge also deals with estates, and in Madison County the probate staff records the documents that move title. The office says plainly that its staff cannot give legal advice, so questions about how to word a deed belong with an attorney or a closing agent.

For a seller, the recording step is the last thing that happens. The title company prepares the deed, collects the recording charges and the deed tax at closing, and files the paperwork.

sections.h2: What are the Madison County recording fees for a deed?
sections.html:
The posted schedule totals $25.75 for the first page of a document and $2.50 for each additional page. The county's own fee page is dated April 1, 2013, so check with the office for any later change before you rely on it for an exact figure.

ChargeAmount
Imaging fee$10.00
Per page$2.50
Filing fee$1.00
Microfilm$0.25
Mental health fee$12.00
Total, first page$25.75
Each additional page$2.50

A three-page deed that carries its own sales validation information would therefore cost $30.75 to record on this schedule, before the deed tax. If a separate validation form is attached, add $2.50 for that page.

sections.h2: How much is the Alabama deed tax in Madison County?
sections.html:
The deed tax is $0.50 for each $500 of value or fraction of $500, which works out to $1.00 per $1,000. Madison County prints it as 50 cents per $500, based on the appraised value or the purchase price, with a minimum of 50 cents if the purchase is 100% financed.

The state statute behind it is section 40-22-1 of the Code of Alabama. It sets the tax at $0.50 for each $500 or fraction in value conveyed, and it taxes only the value above any mortgage or vendor's lien that has already paid mortgage tax. Two thirds of what the probate judge collects goes to the state treasury and one third to the county treasury.

As plain arithmetic from that formula, a sale at $250,000 produces 500 units of $500, so the deed tax is $250. A sale at $180,000 produces 360 units and $180. These are illustrations, not quotes, so your closing agent should run the actual numbers.

Some instruments are exempt. The statute lists transfers of mortgages that already paid mortgage tax, deeds for nominal consideration meant to perfect title, and re-recorded corrected instruments.

sections.h2: What is the RT-1 form and when does Madison County require it?
sections.html:
The RT-1 Real Estate Sales Validation form is required to accompany deeds recorded in Madison County, unless the same information is written into the deed itself. The requirement took effect on August 1, 2012, and the county charges an extra $2.50 page fee when the form is recorded. It does not apply to correction deeds.

State law is the reason. Section 40-22-1 requires proof of the actual purchase price, or the actual value if the property was not sold. The Department of Revenue developed the form, and a person who signs it in good faith is not required to provide more documentation. A person who intentionally refuses to give the proof after a specific request, or gives false proof, owes a penalty of $100 or 25% of the tax due, whichever is greater.

If no proof is offered at all, the probate judge computes the tax from the latest assessment, and the penalty can apply. For sellers, the simplest course is to make sure the settlement statement and the RT-1 show the same price.

sections.h2: What must a document include to be recorded in Madison County?
sections.html:
The county posts a short list of requirements, and a deed that misses one can be rejected at the counter.

  • Original documents are required, and copies from other courts must be certified.
  • Every document must carry the name and address of the person who prepared it.
  • Grantor marital status must appear on all deeds, and mortgagor status on mortgages.
  • Checks are payable to Judge of Probate, Madison County, Alabama.
  • Mailed documents need an adequately sized self-addressed stamped envelope and a 3-inch margin at the top of the first page.

Electronic recording is available through two approved vendors, Simplifile and CSC. E-recording stops at 4 p.m. daily, and the clerks cannot fill in blanks on a document. If two documents have to record in order, such as a deed followed by a second mortgage, the county advises waiting until the first is returned before uploading the next. It also asks you to call before submitting a transaction that spans several counties.

sections.h2: How are names indexed, and what extra charges can appear?
sections.html:
Madison County indexes two grantors, two grantees and two cross-references at no charge, and each additional name or reference costs $1. The county counts more than people toward that limit.

The fee page says the count includes a/k/a and d/b/a names, trusts and trustees, administrators and personal representatives, an estate of a deceased person, MERS, and companies listed as manager, member or partner. An inherited house sold by an estate, or a property owned by an LLC with several managers, can pick up a few of these small charges.

Other items on the posted schedule:

  • Certified copies cost $1 per page plus $2 for certification.
  • Mortgage tax is 15 cents per $100, or $1.50 per $1,000, rounded up to the next $100.
  • Mortgages and deeds to exempt entities carry an additional 50 cent no tax stamp fee.
  • Releases, assignments, affidavits, liens and powers of attorney use the same basic recording fees as deeds.

sections.h2: What changes when a deed and a mortgage are filed together?
sections.html:
When a deed and a mortgage record at the same time, the deed tax is paid on the down payment or equity, not the full price. If the entire price is financed, the deed tax drops to the 50 cent minimum.

The exception is a deed filed with a tax-exempt mortgage, where the deed tax is figured on the full purchase price or appraised value. The county also tells filers to confirm the deed and mortgage consideration in the e-recording system before submitting.

A cash sale is simpler. With no lender, no mortgage tax applies to the buyer's side, and the transaction usually needs only the deed, the validation form and the recording charges.

sections.h2: How does Madison County fit into a Huntsville-area home sale?
sections.html:
Madison County is the second most populous county in Alabama, with 388,153 residents counted in 2020 and about 433,516 estimated for 2025. It was established on December 13, 1808, and Huntsville is its seat.

The housing stock matters when you sell. The 2020 census shows 169,820 housing units, about 7.1% of them vacant, and 33.7% of occupied homes are rented. Redstone Arsenal and the space and defense contractors around it have fed the area's job growth since the 1950s, and the population climbed from 72,903 in 1950 to 388,153 by 2020.

A deed for a Madison County house is not always straightforward. Houses inherited through an estate, homes with tenants, and properties with unpaid taxes all need extra steps, and the probate office is where those steps end.

sections.h2: What documents does a probate-related sale usually need in Madison County?
sections.html:
The probate judge's office handles estates as well as land records, so an heir selling an inherited house may deal with both desks. Ask the office or an attorney which estate papers apply to your situation.

  • The prior deed or title information showing how the owner held the property.
  • Any estate paperwork the office or your attorney says applies, when the owner has died.
  • The deed itself, with preparer details and grantor marital status.
  • The RT-1 or matching price language in the deed.
  • Payment for the recording fee and deed tax.

We buy houses in Madison County as they are, including inherited and tax-delinquent homes.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in Madison County, AL?
faqs.a: At the Judge of Probate in the Madison County Service Center, 1918 Memorial Parkway NW, Huntsville, or electronically through an approved vendor such as Simplifile or CSC.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Madison County?
faqs.a: The posted schedule is $25.75 for the first page and $2.50 for each additional page, plus deed tax. The schedule is dated April 1, 2013, so confirm current charges with the office.

faqs.q: What is the Alabama deed tax?
faqs.a: $0.50 per $500 of value or fraction, which is $1.00 per $1,000, under Code of Alabama section 40-22-1. The minimum is $0.50.

faqs.q: Do I need an RT-1 form in Madison County?
faqs.a: Yes, unless the same information is written into the deed. The form carries an extra $2.50 page fee and does not apply to correction deeds.

faqs.q: Can the probate office help me write a deed?
faqs.a: No. The office says its staff are prohibited by law from giving legal advice, so use an attorney or closing agent.
